terms.meaning: A short explanation of a report written by an artificial intelligence program.
A doorway other programs use to ask this app's server for data.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and setup
sections.what: Loads the parts the screen needs: layout pieces, icons, navigation, shared styles, shared cards and chips, and the API client that fetches the summary.
sections.why: Likely reason: standard setup, with the API client added so the screen can request the summary.

sections.name: LabValue
sections.title: Shape of one lab value
sections.what: Describes what one lab result contains: the measure name, value, unit, normal range, whether it is abnormal, an optional note, and an optional trend.
sections.why: Likely reason: a fixed shape lets the code check the names of fields while it is being written.
sections.watch_out: This shape is checked only when the code is built. Data from the server is trusted as it arrives.

sections.name: AiSummaryData
sections.title: Shape of the whole summary
sections.what: Describes the full summary: plain-language text, clinical text, key findings, risk flags, recommendations, citations and a mock-data flag.
sections.why: Likely reason: groups everything the screen needs into one object.
sections.watch_out: Citations are stored but never shown on this screen.

sections.name: ReportSummaryScreen (part 1)
sections.title: Fetching, converting and sharing the summary
sections.what: Requests the summary for this document and rebuilds it into the shape above, accepting several possible field names from the server and filling gaps with blanks. The share handler builds a short text with the plain summary and key values.
sections.why: Likely reason: the server may use different naming styles, so the app accepts more than one.
sections.watch_out: When the request fails, the error is only written to the log and the user gets no message.

sections.name: ReportSummaryScreen: if
sections.title: Waiting and no-summary views
sections.what: Shows a spinner while the summary loads. If there is no summary, it shows a Summary In Progress message saying that OCR is ready but the AI summary has not been made, with a back button.
sections.why: Likely reason: summaries may be created later, so the screen explains the gap rather than showing an empty page.
sections.watch_out: The same message is shown after a failed request, so an error can look like a normal wait.

sections.name: ReportSummaryScreen (part 3)
sections.title: Header, status chip and key findings
sections.what: Shows back and share buttons, a status chip (Attention Required if there are risk flags, otherwise Mostly Normal), the plain-language summary, then one card per key finding with its value, unit, trend arrow, normal range and interpretation.
sections.why: Likely reason: the most important information comes first, with detail below it.
sections.watch_out: The status chip depends only on risk flags, so it can show Mostly Normal while a finding is marked abnormal.

sections.name: ReportSummaryScreen (part 4)
sections.title: Next steps and disclaimer
sections.what: Shows a list of recommended next steps when there are any, then a note that the summary is AI-generated and is not medical advice.
sections.why: Likely reason: the disclaimer sets expectations about AI-written medical text.
sections.watch_out: The disclaimer is the only warning on this screen, and the screen does not say whether the text came from mock data.

summary: Shows an AI-written, plain-language summary of a lab report, with key values, trend arrows, risk flags and next steps, and lets the user share it.
purpose: Helps a patient understand lab results without reading medical wording, and makes clear that the text is AI-generated.
why: Likely reason: lab reports are hard for patients to read, so the app adds a plain explanation. The disclaimer is shown because the text is produced by AI.
how: When the screen opens it asks the API for the summary of this document. It turns the reply into one fixed shape, accepting several possible field names. While it waits it shows a spinner. If there is no summary it shows a Summary In Progress message. Otherwise it shows a status chip, the plain-language summary, one card per key finding with its trend arrow and interpretation, recommended next steps, and a disclaimer. The share button sends the plain summary and key values through the phone's share options.
inputs: The document ID from the route, and the summary data returned by the API for that document.
outputs: A displayed summary and an optional share message. Nothing is saved on this screen.
risks: A failed request is only logged, so the screen shows the same message as a normal wait. The is_mock flag is read but never shown, so sample AI text can look like a real result. The status chip only checks risk flags, so it can say Mostly Normal while a finding is marked abnormal. Shared text leaves the app and goes wherever the user sends it.
debug: If the screen says the summary is in progress when it should have data, look in the development log for the message from fetchSummary and check the API reply's shape. If the values look like sample data, check whether the server flags them as mock. If the chip contradicts the findings, compare the risk flags with each finding's abnormal marker.
